sanskrit: puruṣādānucaritā bhīrūṇāṃ kaśmalāvahā nadī yodhamahāyajñe tad asyāvabhṛthaṃ smṛtam
english: Haunted by flesh-eating creatures, breeding faintness in cowards—such is the river. In the great sacrifice of war that is held to be the warrior's final ablution.

sanskrit: vedī yasya tv amitrāṇāṃ śirobhir avakīryate aśvaskandhair gajaskandhais tasya lokā yathā mama
english: He whose altar is strewn with the heads of his foes, with the shoulders of horses and the shoulders of elephants—his are worlds such as mine.

sanskrit: patnīśālā kṛtā yasya pareṣāṃ vāhinīmukham havirdhānaṃ svavāhinyas tad asyāhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: He for whom the vanguard of the enemy's host serves as the wife's pavilion, and his own troops as the oblation-shed—so the wise declare.

sanskrit: sadaś cāntarayodhāgnir āgnīdhraś cottarāṃ diśam śatrusenākalatrasya sarvalokān adūrataḥ
english: The assembly-hall is the fire amid the contending warriors, and the priest's fire-shed lies toward the north—the consort of the enemy's army has all the worlds close at hand.

sanskrit: yadā tūbhayato vyūho bhavaty ākāśam agrataḥ sāsya vedī tathā yajñe nityaṃ vedās trayo 'gnayaḥ
english: When the array is drawn up on both sides with open ground in front, that is his altar; and in this sacrifice the three Vedas are ever the three fires.

sanskrit: yas tu yodhaḥ parāvṛttaḥ saṃtrasto hanyate paraiḥ apratiṣṭhaṃ sa narakaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: But the warrior who turns away and, panic-stricken, is slain by his foes goes to a bottomless hell—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yasya śoṇitavegena nadī syāt samabhiplutā keśamāṃsāsthisaṃkīrṇā sa gacchet paramāṃ gatim
english: He by whose surging blood a river is made to overflow, thick with hair and flesh and bone, attains the supreme state.

sanskrit: yas tu senāpatiṃ hatvā tadyānam adhirohati sa viṣṇuvikramakrāmī bṛhaspatisamaḥ kratuḥ
english: He who slays the enemy's commander and mounts his chariot strides with the stride of Viṣṇu; his is a sacrifice equal to that of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: nāyakaṃ vā pramāṇaṃ vā yo vā syāt tatra pūjitaḥ jīvagrāhaṃ nigṛhṇāti tasya lokā yathā mama
english: He who takes captive alive a leader, or a chief authority, or whoever is honored there—his are worlds such as mine.

sanskrit: āhave nihataṃ śūraṃ na śoceta kadā cana aśocyo hi hataḥ śūraḥ svargaloke mahīyate
english: For the hero slain in battle one should never grieve; the slain hero is beyond mourning—he is exalted in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: na hy annaṃ nodakaṃ tasya na snānaṃ nāpy aśaucakam hatasya kartum icchanti tasya lokāñ śṛṇuṣva me
english: For the slain hero men perform no rite of food, no water-offering, no bath, no observance of impurity—hear from me the worlds that are his.

sanskrit: varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi śūram āyodhane hatam tvaramāṇā hi dhāvanti mama bhartā bhaved iti
english: Thousands of choice apsarases rush headlong toward the hero slain in battle, each crying, 'Let him be my husband!'

sanskrit: etat tapaś ca puṇyaṃ ca dharmaś caiva sanātanaḥ catvāraś cāśramās tasya yo yuddhe na palāyate
english: This is austerity, this is merit, this is the eternal dharma, and these are the four stages of life—for the man who does not flee in battle.

sanskrit: vṛddhaṃ balaṃ na hantavyaṃ naiva strī na ca vai dvijaḥ tṛṇapūrṇamukhaś caiva tavāsmīti ca yo vadet
english: The aged force is not to be killed, nor a woman, nor a brāhmaṇa, nor one who takes a blade of grass in his mouth and says, 'I am yours.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ vṛtraṃ balaṃ pākaṃ śatamāyaṃ virocanam durāvāryaṃ ca namuciṃ naikamāyaṃ ca śambaram
english: I slew Vṛtra, Bala, Pāka, Virocana of the hundred wiles, the irresistible Namuci, and Śambara of manifold deceits;

sanskrit: vipracittiṃ ca daiteyaṃ danoḥ putrāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ prahrādaṃ ca nihatyājau tato devādhipo 'bhavam
english: and the Daitya Vipracitti, and all the sons of Danu, and Prahrāda—having slain them in battle, I then became lord of the gods.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity etac chakravacanaṃ niśamya pratigṛhya ca yodhānām ātmanaḥ siddhim ambarīṣo 'bhipannavān
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard and taken to heart this speech of Śakra, Ambarīṣa came to understand the perfection attainable by warriors and by himself.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam pratardano maithilaś ca saṃgrāmaṃ yatra cakratuḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the battle that Pratardana and the king of Mithilā waged together.

sanskrit: yajñopavītī saṃgrāme janako maithilo yathā yodhān uddharṣayām āsa tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Hear, Yudhiṣṭhira, how Janaka of Mithilā, wearing the sacred thread, roused his warriors to ardor upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: janako maithilo rājā mahātmā sarvatattvavit yodhān svān darśayām āsa svargaṃ narakam eva ca
english: King Janaka of Mithilā, the great-souled one who knew all truths, revealed to his warriors both heaven and hell.

sanskrit: abhītānām ime lokā bhāsvanto hanta paśyata pūrṇā gandharvakanyābhiḥ sarvakāmaduho 'kṣayāḥ
english: 'Behold! These shining worlds belong to the fearless—filled with the daughters of the gandharvas, granting every desire, and imperishable.

sanskrit: ime palāyamānānāṃ narakāḥ pratyupasthitāḥ akīrtiḥ śāśvatī caiva patitavyam anantaram
english: And these hells stand ready for those who flee—everlasting infamy, and a fall to follow at once.'

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvārīn vijayato bhūtvā saṃtyāgabuddhayaḥ narakasyāpratiṣṭhasya mā bhūta vaśavartinaḥ
english: 'Seeing those foes, conquer them, your minds resolved upon self-surrender; do not fall under the sway of the bottomless hell.

sanskrit: tyāgamūlaṃ hi śūrāṇāṃ svargadvāram anuttamam ity uktās te nṛpatinā yodhāḥ parapuraṃjaya
english: For self-sacrifice is the root of heroes' unsurpassed gateway to heaven.' So addressed by the king, O conqueror of enemy cities, those warriors—

sanskrit: vyajayanta raṇe śatrūn harṣayanto janeśvaram tasmād ātmavatā nityaṃ sthātavyaṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: —vanquished their foes in the fray, gladdening their lord of men. Therefore the self-possessed man should ever stand firm at the head of battle.

sanskrit: gajānāṃ rathino madhye rathānām anu sādinaḥ sādinām antarā sthāpyaṃ pādātam iha daṃśitam
english: Amid the elephants the chariot-warriors, behind the chariots the horsemen, and between the horsemen the mailed foot-soldiers should be stationed.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ vyūhate rājā sa nityaṃ jayate dviṣaḥ tasmād evaṃ vidhātavyaṃ nityam eva yudhiṣṭhira
english: The king who arrays his forces thus ever conquers his enemies; therefore it should always be ordered in this way, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sarve sukṛtam icchantaḥ suyuddhenātimanyavaḥ kṣobhayeyur anīkāni sāgaraṃ makarā iva
english: All, desiring merit, full of fierce wrath through good fighting, would shake the enemy ranks as sea-monsters churn the ocean.

sanskrit: harṣayeyur viṣaṇṇāṃś ca vyavasthāpya parasparam jitāṃ ca bhūmiṃ rakṣeta bhagnān nātyanusārayet
english: They should cheer the dejected and steady one another; one should guard the ground that has been won, and not pursue the routed too far.

sanskrit: punarāvartamānānāṃ nirāśānāṃ ca jīvite na vegaḥ susaho rājaṃs tasmān nātyanusārayet
english: The onset of men who turn back to fight and have despaired of life cannot easily be withstood, O king; therefore do not pursue too far.

sanskrit: na hi prahartum icchanti śūrāḥ prādravatāṃ bhayāt tasmāt palāyamānānāṃ kuryān nātyanusāraṇam
english: For heroes have no wish to strike those who run off in fear; therefore one should not press the pursuit of those who flee.

sanskrit: carāṇām acarā hy annam adaṃṣṭrā daṃṣṭriṇām api apāṇayaḥ pāṇimatām annaṃ śūrasya kātarāḥ
english: The motionless are food for the moving, the fangless for the fanged, the handless for those who have hands—and cowards are food for the hero.

sanskrit: samānapṛṣṭhodarapāṇipādāḥ; paścāc chūraṃ bhīravo 'nuvrajanti ato bhayārtāḥ praṇipatya bhūyaḥ; kṛtvāñjalīn upatiṣṭhanti śūrān
english: Though equal in back and belly, in hand and foot, cowards follow the hero from behind; and so, tormented by fear, bowing low and folding their hands, they wait upon the brave.

sanskrit: śūrabāhuṣu loko 'yaṃ lambate putravat sadā tasmāt sarvāsv avasthāsu śūraḥ saṃmānam arhati
english: Upon the arms of heroes this world ever leans, as a child upon its parent; therefore in every circumstance the hero deserves honor.

sanskrit: na hi śauryāt paraṃ kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate śūraḥ sarvaṃ pālayati sarvaṃ śūre pratiṣṭhitam
english: For in the three worlds there is nothing higher than valor; the hero protects all, and upon the hero all things rest.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yathā jayārthinaḥ senāṃ nayanti bharatarṣabha īṣad dharmaṃ prapīḍyāpi tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How those who seek victory lead an army, even by straining dharma a little—tell me that, O grandfather, bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca satyena hi sthitā dharmā upapattyā tathāpare sādhvācāratayā ke cit tathaivaupayikā api upāyadharmān vakṣyāmi siddhārthān arthadharmayoḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Some duties rest upon truth, others upon sound reasoning, some upon the conduct of the good, and some upon expediency. I shall expound the duties of expedient means, which fulfill the aims of both profit and dharma.

sanskrit: nirmaryādā dasyavas tu bhavanti paripanthinaḥ teṣāṃ prativighātārthaṃ pravakṣyāmy atha naigamam kāryāṇāṃ saṃprasiddhyarthaṃ tān upāyān nibodha me
english: Lawless brigands become highway-robbers; to counter them I shall set forth the established usage. Learn from me those expedients for the accomplishment of one's ends.

sanskrit: ubhe prajñe veditavye ṛjvī vakrā ca bhārata jānan vakrāṃ na seveta pratibādheta cāgatām
english: Two kinds of wisdom must be known, O Bhārata—the straight and the crooked. Knowing the crooked, one should not practice it, yet should repel it when it comes.

sanskrit: amitrā eva rājānaṃ bhedenopacaranty uta tāṃ rājā nikṛtiṃ jānan yathāmitrān prabādhate
english: Enemies indeed approach a king through the sowing of dissension; knowing that deceit, the king beats them back as he would foes.

sanskrit: gajānāṃ pārśvacarmāṇi govṛṣājagarāṇi ca śalyakaṅkaṭalohāni tanutrāṇi matāni ca
english: The flank-hides of elephants, of bulls and great serpents, porcupine-quill plate and iron—these are reckoned as body-armor.

sanskrit: śitapītāni śastrāṇi saṃnāhāḥ pītalohitāḥ nānārañjanaraktāḥ syuḥ patākāḥ ketavaś ca te
english: The weapons should be sharpened and burnished, the coats of mail tawny-red, and the pennants and standards dyed in many colors.

sanskrit: ṛṣṭayas tomarāḥ khaḍgā niśitāś ca paraśvadhāḥ phalakāny atha carmāṇi pratikalpyāny anekaśaḥ abhinītāni śastrāṇi yodhāś ca kṛtaniśramāḥ
english: Swords, lances, blades, and whetted battle-axes, shields and bucklers—these are to be prepared in great numbers; the weapons well-tempered, and the warriors well-trained.

sanskrit: caitryāṃ vā mārgaśīrṣyāṃ vā senāyogaḥ praśasyate pakvasasyā hi pṛthivī bhavaty ambumatī tathā
english: The mustering of the army is commended in the month of Caitra or of Mārgaśīrṣa, for then the earth bears ripened grain and abundant water.

sanskrit: naivātiśīto nātyuṣṇaḥ kālo bhavati bhārata tasmāt tadā yojayeta pareṣāṃ vyasaneṣu vā eteṣu yogāḥ senāyāḥ praśastāḥ parabādhane
english: The season then is neither too cold nor too hot, O Bhārata; therefore one should mobilize at that time, or in the seasons of the enemy's distress—such occasions for marshaling an army are commended for harrying the foe.

sanskrit: jalavāṃs tṛṇavān mārgaḥ samo gamyaḥ praśasyate cārair hi vihitābhyāsaḥ kuśalair vanagocaraiḥ
english: A road with water and grass, level and passable, is to be preferred—one well reconnoitered beforehand by skilled scouts versed in the forests.

sanskrit: navyāraṇyair na śakyeta gantuṃ mṛgagaṇair iva tasmāt sarvāsu senāsu yojayanti jayārthinaḥ
english: Through fresh wildwoods it would be no more possible to march than for herds of deer; therefore those who seek victory employ scouts in every army.

sanskrit: āvāsas toyavān durgaḥ paryākāśaḥ praśasyate pareṣām upasarpāṇāṃ pratiṣedhas tathā bhavet
english: A camp that has water, is hard of access, and has open ground around it is commended, for thereby the enemy's infiltrators are repulsed.

sanskrit: ākāśaṃ tu vanābhyāśe manyante guṇavattaram bahubhir guṇajātais tu ye yuddhakuśalā janāḥ
english: But open ground near a forest is held more advantageous, on account of its many merits, by men skilled in war.

sanskrit: upanyāso 'pasarpāṇāṃ padātīnāṃ ca gūhanam atha śatrupratīghātam āpadarthaṃ parāyaṇam
english: The posting of spies, the concealment of foot-soldiers, the repelling of the enemy, and a refuge against calamity—

sanskrit: saptarṣīn pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā yudhyerann acalā iva anena vidhinā rājañ jigīṣetāpi durjayān
english: —placing the Seven Sages at their back, they would fight unshaken as mountains. By this method, O king, one may seek to conquer even the unconquerable.

sanskrit: yato vāyur yataḥ sūryo yataḥ śukras tato jayaḥ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ jyāya eṣāṃ saṃnipāte yudhiṣṭhira
english: Where the wind is, where the sun is, where Śukra is—there is victory; and of these, each former is the more important when they meet, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: akardamām anudakām amaryādām aloṣṭakām aśvabhūmiṃ praśaṃsanti ye yuddhakuśalā janāḥ
english: Free of mire, free of water, unbounded, free of clods—such ground for cavalry men skilled in war commend.

sanskrit: samā nirudakākāśā rathabhūmiḥ praśasyate nīcadrumā mahākakṣā sodakā hastiyodhinām
english: Level, waterless, and open ground is commended for chariots; ground with low trees, tall grass, and water is for those who fight on elephants.

sanskrit: bahudurgā mahāvṛkṣā vetraveṇubhir āstṛtā padātīnāṃ kṣamā bhūmiḥ parvatopavanāni ca
english: Ground full of fastnesses, great trees, overspread with reeds and bamboo, and the mountains and groves—such terrain is fit for foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: padātibahulā senā dṛḍhā bhavati bhārata rathāśvabahulā senā sudineṣu praśasyate
english: An army rich in foot-soldiers is steadfast, O Bhārata; an army rich in chariots and horses is commended in fair weather.

sanskrit: padātināgabahulā prāvṛṭkāle praśasyate guṇān etān prasaṃkhyāya deśakālau prayojayet
english: One rich in foot-soldiers and elephants is commended in the rainy season. Weighing these qualities, one should make use of place and time.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintya yo yāti tithinakṣatrapūjitaḥ vijayaṃ labhate nityaṃ senāṃ samyak prayojayan
english: He who, having pondered thus, marches forth, honoring the lunar day and the asterism, ever wins victory, marshaling his army aright.

sanskrit: prasuptāṃs tṛṣitāñ śrāntān prakīrṇān nābhighātayet mokṣe prayāṇe calane pānabhojanakālayoḥ
english: One should not strike those asleep, thirsty, weary, or scattered, nor at the time of release, of march, of movement, or of drinking and eating.

sanskrit: atikṣiptān vyatikṣiptān vihatān pratanūkṛtān suvisrambhān kṛtārambhān upanyāsapratāpitān bahiścarān upanyāsān kṛtvā veśmānusāriṇaḥ
english: Those flung far off, those scattered apart, those struck down, those reduced to small numbers, those grown over-confident, those engaged in some undertaking, those inflamed by intrigue—having set spies abroad as agents who follow them to their dwellings—

sanskrit: pāraṃparyāgate dvāre ye ke cid anuvartinaḥ paricaryāvaroddhāro ye ca ke cana valginaḥ
english: —at the gate that has come down by tradition, whoever are the attendants, the warders of service, and whatever bold and dashing men there are—

sanskrit: anīkaṃ ye prabhindanti bhinnaṃ ye sthagayanti ca samānāśanapānās te kāryā dviguṇavetanāḥ
english: —those who break the enemy's ranks and those who close up a broken line—these are to be given equal food and drink and double wages.

sanskrit: daśādhipatayaḥ kāryāḥ śatādhipatayas tathā teṣāṃ sahasrādhipatiṃ kuryāc chūram atandritam
english: Captains over ten should be appointed, and likewise captains over a hundred; and over them one should set as captain of a thousand a hero who is never slothful.

sanskrit: yathāmukhyaṃ saṃnipātya vaktavyāḥ sma śapāmahe yathā jayārthaṃ saṃgrāme na jahyāma parasparam
english: Assembling them by rank of precedence, one should say: 'Let us swear that for the sake of victory in battle we shall not forsake one another.

sanskrit: ihaiva te nivartantāṃ ye naḥ ke cana bhīravaḥ na ghātayeyuḥ pradaraṃ kurvāṇās tumule sati
english: Let any cowards among us turn back here and now, lest by making a breach in the uproar of battle they get us killed.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ ca svapakṣaṃ ca palāyan hanti saṃyuge dravyanāśo vadho 'kīrtir ayaśaś ca palāyane
english: He who flees in combat destroys both himself and his own side; in flight there is loss of property, slaughter, infamy, and disgrace.

sanskrit: amanojñāsukhā vācaḥ puruṣasya palāyataḥ pratispandauṣṭhadantasya nyastasarvāyudhasya ca
english: Ugly and joyless are the words of the man who flees, his lips and teeth quivering, all his weapons cast aside.

sanskrit: hitvā palāyamānasya sahāyān prāṇasaṃśaye amitrair anubaddhasya dviṣatām astu nas tathā
english: As for him who flees, abandoning his comrades when their lives hang in the balance, hemmed in by his foes—let such a fate be our enemies', not ours.

sanskrit: manuṣyāpasadā hy ete ye bhavanti parāṅmukhāḥ rāśivardhanamātrās te naiva te pretya no iha
english: For those who turn their backs are the dregs of men; they merely swell the heap of the dead, gaining nothing here or hereafter.

sanskrit: amitrā hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pratyudyānti palāyinam jayinaṃ suhṛdas tāta vandanair maṅgalena ca
english: With glad hearts the enemies go out to meet the man who flees; but friends, my son, greet the victor with salutations and with blessings.

sanskrit: yasya sma vyasane rājann anumodanti śatravaḥ tad asahyataraṃ duḥkham ahaṃ manye vadhād api
english: He at whose misfortune, O king, his enemies rejoice—that, I deem, is a sorrow harder to bear even than death.'

sanskrit: śriyaṃ jānīta dharmasya mūlaṃ sarvasukhasya ca sā bhīrūṇāṃ parān yāti śūras tām adhigacchati
english: 'Know prosperity to be the root of dharma and of all happiness; from cowards she passes to others, but the hero attains her.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ svargam icchantaḥ saṃgrāme tyaktajīvitāḥ jayanto vadhyamānā vā prāptum arhāma sadgatim
english: We, then, longing for heaven, our lives laid down in battle, whether conquering or being slain, deserve to win the goodly path.'

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃśaptaśapathāḥ samabhityaktajīvitāḥ amitravāhinīṃ vīrāḥ saṃpragāhanty abhīravaḥ
english: Thus having sworn their oath together, having wholly given up their lives, the fearless heroes plunge into the enemy's host.

sanskrit: agrataḥ puruṣānīkam asicarmavatāṃ bhavet pṛṣṭhataḥ śakaṭānīkaṃ kalatraṃ madhyatas tathā
english: In front should be a phalanx of men bearing sword and shield, behind a line of wagons, and the noncombatants in the middle.

sanskrit: pareṣāṃ pratighātārthaṃ padātīnāṃ ca gūhanam api hy asmin pare gṛddhā bhaveyur ye purogamāḥ
english: For repelling the enemy and concealing the foot-soldiers; for upon this the foe would grow greedy—those of them who advance in the van.

sanskrit: ye purastād abhimatāḥ sattvavanto manasvinaḥ te pūrvam abhivarteraṃs tān anvag itare janāḥ
english: Those esteemed for the front rank, courageous and high-spirited, should advance first, and the rest of the men close behind them.

sanskrit: api coddharṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ bhīrūṇām api yatnataḥ skandhadarśanamātraṃ tu tiṣṭheyur vā samīpataḥ
english: And even the cowards should be roused to ardor with effort; or let them at least stand close by, merely showing their shoulders.

sanskrit: saṃhatān yodhayed alpān kāmaṃ vistārayed bahūn sūcīmukham anīkaṃ syād alpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha
english: A small force one should make fight in close formation, but a large one may be spread out at will; against a numerous foe, a small force's array should be needle-pointed.

sanskrit: saṃprayuddhe prahṛṣṭe vā satyaṃ vā yadi vānṛtam pragṛhya bāhūn krośeta bhagnā bhagnāḥ parā iti
english: When the battle is joined, or when spirits are high, whether it be true or false, one should raise his arms and cry aloud, 'The enemy are broken, broken!'
